cells.tense: What began as open possibility is finished and real, and you are the one bearing it now.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Pick one direction out of the several your finished work could take, and follow it this week — a single route, taken and held.
cells.core:
You finished something that began as nothing but possibility, and now you carry the weight of what it turned into. Where what's out of proportion gets set back to even, the question stops being whether it was fair to start — that's behind you — and becomes which way this real thing leans now. Under the load, holding every route open another season feels like keeping the options intact. What it actually keeps is the one thing a decision buys: nothing gets your whole weight behind it.

So choose a route and travel it. Of everything this finished work could become next, take one direction this week and stay with it — not both, not one for now with another tucked away. The pull is yours to name and follow. What you buy for taking one route is your full force moving the same way as the thing you made.
cells.sheetLine: The point of finishing is you get to decide what it means now.
cells.verb: carrying what pure possibility became, to its end
cells.place: where what's out of proportion gets set back to even

cells.tense: You are bracing at a future that hasn't arrived, passing judgment on outcomes still forming.
cells.act: describe what is in front of your eyes in five plain lines, no conclusions
cells.ask: Take something within reach — a room, a message, a bill — and write five lines of pure description, no verdicts on what any of it means.
cells.core:
Bracing is what this thing does when the load gets heavy. Nearby, something sits out of proportion, and you've already ruled — already seen where it lands, already acted as if the ending had happened. Fairness delivered before the facts isn't fairness; it's a verdict read before the trial finished, and the rush is the whole of what's wrong with it.

Looking has to come before ruling, and it can't be skipped. Take one thing actually within reach and write five lines describing only what's there — colour, sound, the words someone used, what's open and what's shut. No conclusions at the end. You'll describe most of what you were about to rule on, and the ruling will arrive after you've looked, which is where it belongs.
cells.sheetLine: You can't recalibrate what you haven't looked at first.

cells.tense: Something was finished and you are still standing at the door you already walked through.
cells.act: sit somewhere new with nothing in your hands and let whatever comes, come
cells.ask: Find a spot you've never sat, leave phone and task behind, and stay a while — long enough for something to arrive without being fetched.
cells.core:
The completion already happened. What began as pure possibility ran its course and became real, and by the balance of things you'd be carrying it forward. Instead you're standing in the doorway, the load uncollected, waiting on a verdict about whether it counted — and while the wait goes on, the part of you that should be weighing what's next has nothing current on the scale. The fairness you keep checking for isn't being decided by anyone. It was settled when the work finished.

Receiving opens this, not pushing — effort can't be forced into an empty vessel. Sit somewhere new, hands empty, and let whatever comes, come. Nothing has to be decided there and nothing has to be felt on schedule; you're only making space. The load you've been waiting to pick up is in that spot, and it hands itself over when the noise drops.
cells.sheetLine: The completion happened. You're waiting for permission nobody is holding.

cells.tense: You are already balancing what lies between people, while telling yourself you aren't the one doing it.
cells.act: let the vision be shared with one other
cells.ask: Pick one person and one project, and speak the whole direction aloud to them — the aim, the why, the next move, said as yours.
cells.core:
The balancing is happening because you're doing it. The word shifted here, the weight taken there, the thing kept fair between two people and credited to circumstance or to the other person's good sense — you're the hand, and the story you tell about the hand is that it wasn't there. The connection you'd say simply formed is one you formed. Where what's out of proportion gets set back to even, an author who won't sign the work can't correct it or repeat it on purpose.

So let one person in on the direction. Choose someone and something you're building, and tell them the whole of it — the aim, the why, the next move — described as yours, out loud. What you say to them you can no longer keep off your own record. What ran you silently becomes something you carry with someone, and a connection carried in the open can be chosen again tomorrow, deliberately, by the one who built it.
cells.sheetLine: The hand keeping things fair is yours. Say so out loud.

cells.place: where what's out of proportion gets set back to even
